purpose: Install newly represented approved but uninstalled Physalis and Persicaria species, using the October 14 scientific diagnostic reviews and independently licensed exact-species research grade first images. No county native-range audit; provisional photographs only; leave Persicaria bicornis separate due to unresolved close identity.

selected.look_here_first: Find the papery ochrea sheath at each swollen node; inspect the nearly smooth flower spikes, then check two styles and flattened biconvex mature achenes.
Examine the papery ochrea and its relatively long rim bristles; verify branching rhizomes, then count three styles and inspect three-angled achenes.
Look at the swollen stem nodes with papery ochrea, then inspect flower clusters and anchor-forked veins of the outer tepals under magnification.
Find the papery ochrea at nodes; compare mature achenes and multiple flowers with Persicaria bicornis rather than deciding from one leaf or flower.
Inspect the papery inflated fruit calyx, then check branched stellate hairs with a hand lens, rhizomes, and corolla markings.
Inspect inflated fruit calyx and perennial rhizomes; look for sparse forward-pointing SIMPLE hairs rather than the branched hairs of P. cinerascens.
Look for the tiny urn-shaped flower, short flower stalk and five-ribbed husk, unlike the broad corollas and typically ten-ribbed husks of most groundcherries.
